search_log: Searched "The Man with the Golden Arm" Nelson Algren excerpt, first chapter, and read an extract; opened the New Republic opening, the page-69 interior excerpt, publisher pages, and a sustained transcription.
Searched the verified title with point of view, narrator, third person, third-person, and omniscient; found the MidAmerica scholarly analysis and the Writing Fiction craft discussion.
Searched the title with epistolary, diary, letters, frame narrative, multiple narrators, and alternating point of view; found no credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections.
Checked Seven Stories Press and Google Books publisher records; they verified the work and edition but supplied synopsis or introductory material rather than diagnostic novel narration.
Checked Open Library and Internet Archive discovery records; borrowing metadata verified the 1949 Doubleday edition, but accessible search results did not expose a usable sustained excerpt.

Inspected the transcription at the opening, the Part Two boundary, multiple interior locations, and the ending; the base narration remains third person, while the final coroner transcript and first-plural epitaph are local codas rather than alternate base narration.
person_note: The controlling narrator is a nonparticipating third-person voice that shifts focalization among Frankie, Captain Bednar, Sophie, Sparrow, and other characters. Diagnostic Goodreads passages q00026, q00038, and q00041 independently agree with the scholarly whole-book discussion and web passages from the opening, page 69, both parts, and the ending. First-person forms in the quote set are dialogue or paratext. The closing witness transcript and first-plural epitaph are documentary and poetic codas, not sustained first-person base sections. No credible evidence of alternating narration was found; the only minor limitation is the absence of an explicit whole-book POV statement from the publisher itself.
